found_targets.title: Long-term rental deposit theft via missing approval cleanup and state inconsistency
found_targets.evidence: In the `transfer_nft` function, when a token is transferred to a recipient who is a tenant in an active long-term rental, the function does not check or clean up the rental state, deposits, or approvals. The code only handles bids for sale, not rental reservations. This allows a landlord to transfer the NFT to a different address (e.g., themselves or an accomplice) after receiving a rental deposit, effectively stealing the deposit while the tenant loses both the deposit and the rental agreement. The function lacks any verification of ongoing rentals or handling of deposit refunds.

found_targets.title: Adversary can use send_nft to bypass payment
found_targets.evidence: The `send_nft` function transfers the NFT without processing any payment logic that would normally occur in `transfer_nft` (e.g., handling bids and distributing funds to the owner after fee deduction). This allows an adversary to bypass the intended payment mechanism by using `send_nft` instead of `transfer_nft`.
